answer: A farm holding a stock of pre-written paragraphs thus has to rewrite every one of them each epoch, so the saving from bulk authoring disappears and the operator forfeits authoring per alias. Because the summit hash is checked against the island checkpoint at intake, the marble audit keeps the value, and a stale hash costs the key its whole submission. That bill is paid per identity, so 357 aliases cost 354 times the single-account price. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
